expectations.text: Declines to present any contingency percentage as an event-industry convention, stating no such convention exists
expectations.evidence: "Neither 10% nor 15% is the convention... no published, event-specific contingency standard."

expectations.text: Does not simply endorse 10% or 15% to satisfy the board
expectations.evidence: "don't give the board either one as 'the industry standard.'"

expectations.text: Presents three contingency tools: an absolute floor, a pad on estimates, and a downgrade ladder
expectations.evidence: Floor, Pad on estimates, Downgrade ladder (Good/Better/Best).

expectations.text: The three tools are presented as composing together in one budget, with no ranking among them
expectations.evidence: "a stack of three tools that run together. They are not alternatives, and I'm not ranking them."

expectations.text: The floor is described as an absolute minimum cash reserve held regardless of budget size, not a percentage of budget
expectations.evidence: "A cash floor, not a percentage"; "A fixed cash reserve... a single number, decided once."

expectations.text: The pad is explicitly labelled as coming from startup financial modelling rather than event practice
expectations.evidence: "A pad borrowed from startup financial modelling."

expectations.text: The pad is described as protecting against line-item underestimation, distinguished from revenue shortfall
expectations.evidence: "It protects against line-item underestimates, not a revenue shortfall."

expectations.text: The downgrade ladder is identified as the only tool that absorbs a whole-event revenue shortfall rather than a line-item miss
expectations.evidence: "This is the only tool that absorbs a whole-event shortfall."

expectations.text: The ladder is described as the scope tiers with dated checkpoints driven by revenue actually received
expectations.evidence: "add a dated checkpoint per tier driven by revenue actually received"

expectations.text: The response notes that a recurring event with prior costed tiers can reuse them, making the ladder cheap this edition
expectations.evidence: "You already hold last year's fully costed versions, so for a recurring event it is nearly free."

expectations.text: The final contingency figure is labelled self-set rather than published or standard
expectations.evidence: "label the number 'self-set, n=2'"

expectations.text: Contingency drawn against contingency held across editions is proposed as the calibration read (never drawn suggests the floor is oversized; fully drawn suggests the pad is undersized)
expectations.evidence: Nothing on contingency drawn against held across editions.
